topic: Date.parse: date-only ISO strings are UTC, date-time strings without an offset are local time (MDN)
text:
new Date("2019-01-01") and new Date("2019-01-01T00:00:00") look like the same moment. They aren't.

Per MDN, a date-only ISO string is parsed as UTC. A date-time string with no offset is parsed as local time.

So in a timezone behind UTC, the first one can print as December 31 on your screen.

My rule of thumb:
1. Date-only value (birthday, due date)? Keep it as a string, don't turn it into a Date.
2. A real moment in time? Send it with an explicit offset, like 2019-01-01T00:00:00Z.
3. Never rely on the bare date-time form.

MDN also names Date.parse() inconsistencies as one motivation for the Temporal API.

Which date bug has cost you the most debugging time?
